title: Publish the runner recovery, evidence and Claude observation surfaces on the @moe/runner root
description:
Objective: publish three committed-but-unreachable @moe/runner subtrees on the package root so J3's launcher and restart boundary can be composed against them. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09, verified symbol by symbol on disk. This is the FIFTH instance of one recurring defect; the prior four are the template: task-8ee125d0 (@moe/scheduler, 239aa4f), task-53680e91 (@moe/runner supervisor), task-6054520b (@moe/daemon), and the bridge sweeps.

WHY THIS EXISTS. `packages/runner/package.json` pins `"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}` - an EXCLUSIVE map, so no deep subpath import reaches around it at runtime or under moduleResolution NodeNext. `packages/runner/src/index.ts` publishes artifacts/, scope/, supervisor/ and workspace/ (126 specifiers) but NOT recovery/, NOT evidence/, and NOT providers/claude/. Those three subtrees are committed, tested and completely unreachable from outside the package.

MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09, the unpublished surface:
  recovery/ - classifyCrash, admitSuccessorOverlap, admitResume, advanceRecoveryDrain; types CrashClassification, OverlapVerdict, ResumeVerdict, DrainAdvance; vocabularies RECOVERY_CONTRACT_VERSION, RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS, RECOVERY_LAYERS, RECOVERY_ERROR_CODES, PREDECESSOR_RELEASES
  evidence/ - buildEvidenceReceipt, buildVerificationRecipe, recipeSealMatches, rematerializeCandidate, canonicalObligations, observedExecutionRejection; types EvidenceReceipt, VerificationRecipe, CandidateTreePort, RematerializeCandidateInput/Result, ObservedVerifierExecution, ObservedOutput, ExecutionDisposition; vocabularies VERIFICATION_RECIPE_VERSION, EVIDENCE_RECEIPT_VERSION, EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS, EXECUTION_DISPOSITIONS and the MAX_EVIDENCE_* limits
  providers/claude/ - reconcileClaudeRun, ClaudeProcessExit, ClaudeReconciliation, CLAUDE_RECONCILED_OUTCOMES, CLAUDE_RECONCILIATION_VERSION, plus the capability profile surface (CLAUDE_CAPABILITIES, CLAUDE_CAPABILITY_STATUSES, CLAUDE_PROOF_METHODS, CLAUDE_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_VERSION)

THIS BLOCKS J3. The Foundation canary reports that runner/Claude observation and recovery helpers are "not composed into a real launcher/restart boundary". They cannot be: a consumer outside @moe/runner cannot import them at all. Publishing is the prerequisite; the composition itself is a separate follow-on task.

Deliverable: a curated named-export block in packages/runner/src/index.ts, in the style the file already uses - named exports grouped per module, types in the same block via the `type` modifier, every specifier carrying the .js extension per NodeNext. Read the modules and name only what a consumer needs to classify a crash, admit or refuse a successor overlap and a resume, advance a drain, build and verify an evidence receipt and verification recipe, rematerialize a candidate, and reconcile an observed Claude run. Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *` so the published seam stays a reviewed decision.

NOT in scope: changing ANY behaviour in any runner module; exporting test-only modules (recovery-test-fixtures.ts, evidence fixtures, claude-probe test helpers - all stay internal); the J3 launcher/restart composition itself; touching apps/daemon; any package.json or lockfile edit.

Hard dependencies: none. Every symbol above is committed at HEAD.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/index.ts and packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts (extend the existing surface test).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck
definitionOfDone: packages/runner/src/index.ts exports the recovery, evidence and Claude observation surfaces such that a consumer can, with NO deep subpath import, classify a crash, admit or refuse a successor overlap and a resume, advance a recovery drain, build and seal-verify a verification recipe, build an evidence receipt, rematerialize a candidate, and reconcile an observed Claude run — naming every parameter type and every union branch of every exported function's return type.

The existing packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts is extended to import the package ROOT specifier @moe/runner (never a relative or deep path) and assert per new symbol that the export is present and of the expected typeof, so a dropped export fails by name rather than by a vague count.

The test's set-equality assertion against a hand-written expected export-name list is updated to cover the new symbols, so both a removed export AND an unreviewed addition still go red. The list is hand-transcribed from the modules, never derived from the namespace under test.

Discriminated unions survive publication: for CrashClassification, OverlapVerdict, ResumeVerdict, DrainAdvance and the evidence result unions, a test obtains real values through the published root and asserts each branch is distinguishable by its discriminant — asserted against the production surface, not a locally re-declared type.
No test-only module is exported — recovery-test-fixtures.ts and any evidence or claude test helper stay internal — asserted by the set-equality list.

Zero behaviour change: git diff shows packages/runner/src/index.ts as the only modified non-test file, no .js bridge is added or removed, and the pre-existing runner suite passes with a test count greater than or equal to the pre-task count, stated as an explicit before/after number.
pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck all exit 0, and committed paths are exactly the two owned files.
taskRails: Re-export only. This task changes what is REACHABLE, never what any function DOES. No .ts file other than index.ts may be edited. If a symbol seems to need a signature change to be exportable, report_blocked rather than editing a runner module.

Read the modules before naming a single symbol and do not copy names from this description without verifying each on disk — recovery/, evidence/ and providers/claude/ landed from three different tasks within days of each other.
Never export a test-only module. recovery-test-fixtures.ts and the evidence/claude test helpers stay internal; exporting fixtures puts test code on the runtime surface.
Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *`, so the published seam stays a reviewed decision rather than whatever the modules happen to export next week.
Assert against the production surface obtained through the @moe/runner root import, never against a locally re-declared type or fixture copy.

index.ts already carries 126 specifiers and will grow substantially. Keep it focused: if it passes 250 lines, extract per-area re-export modules (e.g. a recovery surface module) that index.ts re-exports, rather than letting the entry point sprawl past 400.
Any new module created by an extraction needs its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — @moe/runner is bridged and is covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — git commit -- packages/runner/src/index.ts packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts. Several agents share this working directory; verify with git show --stat afterwards.

implementationPlan.description: Re-verify the three subtrees and check for name collisions before composing anything. Read every non-test module under recovery/, evidence/ and providers/claude/ and record each exported value and type — these landed from three different tasks within days of each other, so this task's description may already be stale. TWO CHECKS THAT MUST HAPPEN NOW rather than at compile time. First, DUPLICATE NAMES: evidence/ and recovery/ both define failure and layer vocabularies, and a name exported from two modules is a compile error in index.ts that reads like a mystery; list every name and find collisions. If two modules genuinely export the same identifier, report it as a finding rather than papering over it with a rename in index.ts, which would make the published name differ from the module's own. Second, TEST-ONLY MODULES: identify recovery-test-fixtures.ts and any evidence or claude test helper, and mark them as never-export. Then read the existing packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts from task-53680e91 to reuse its root-import and set-equality pattern rather than inventing a second idiom. Produce no code.

Hand-transcribe the expected export-name list — a separate step because DoD 3 lives or dies on it. Write the complete list of names index.ts will publish, taken BY HAND from the module sources read in step 1, and record it in the step note. Do NOT generate it from Object.keys of any namespace and do not derive it from the export block you are about to write: a list derived from the thing under test asserts only that the namespace equals itself and can never fail (mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself). Scope the list deliberately rather than exporting everything — name what a consumer needs to classify a crash, admit or refuse a successor overlap and a resume, advance a drain, build and seal-verify a recipe, build an evidence receipt, rematerialize a candidate, and reconcile an observed Claude run. Internal helpers that no consumer needs stay internal; publishing them widens the package's public API permanently. This list is simultaneously the specification for step 3 and the expected value for step 4.

Add the three curated export blocks to packages/runner/src/index.ts, matching the file's existing style exactly: one grouped `export { ... } from "./<dir>/<module>.js";` block per module, values first and `type` entries in the same braces, every specifier carrying the .js extension per NodeNext. Export exactly the names on the step-2 list — no blanket `export *`, which would publish whatever these modules happen to export next week and would defeat the set-equality assertion that makes this seam a reviewed decision. Export NO test-only module. THEN MEASURE: index.ts already carries 126 specifiers, so check its line count with wc -l after the additions. If it passes the 250-line target, extract per-area re-export modules (for example a recovery surface module and an evidence surface module) that index.ts re-exports, rather than letting the entry point sprawl toward the 400 hard cap — and give any extracted module its sibling .js bridge in the SAME commit, since @moe/runner is bridged and is now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate.

Extend packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts — DoD 2 and DoD 3. Every assertion imports the package ROOT specifier @moe/runner; never a relative or deep path, since the entire point of this task is that deep subpaths do not resolve through an exclusive exports map. Assert per new symbol that the export is present and of the expected typeof, so a dropped export fails BY NAME rather than by a vague count. Then update the set-equality assertion between Object.keys of the namespace and the hand-written list from step 2, so a removed export AND an unreviewed addition both go red. Assert explicitly that no test-only module leaked onto the surface — recovery-test-fixtures and any evidence or claude helper must be absent from the namespace, which the set-equality check gives you for free provided the hand-written list omits them.

Prove the discriminated unions survive publication — DoD 4, and the known failure mode on this seam. These three subtrees are union-heavy: CrashClassification, OverlapVerdict, ResumeVerdict, DrainAdvance, the evidence build results (BuildEvidenceReceiptResult, RematerializeCandidateResult) and the Claude reconciliation outcomes. A consumer that cannot narrow them by discriminant cannot use them at all, and the supervisor publish task had to fix exactly this for LifecycleOutcome, so it is a demonstrated risk rather than a hypothetical. Obtain real values by CALLING the exported functions through the root import — classifyCrash, admitSuccessorOverlap, admitResume, advanceRecoveryDrain, buildEvidenceReceipt, rematerializeCandidate, reconcileClaudeRun — with inputs that produce each branch, and assert each branch is distinguishable by its discriminant. Do NOT construct union literals to test this: a hand-built literal typechecks regardless of what was published, so it would pass even if the type were unreachable. Assert against the production surface, never a locally re-declared type.

Prove zero behaviour change and run the full gate. Confirm with `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` that packages/runner/src/index.ts is the ONLY modified non-test file — plus any re-export module extracted in step 3 and its bridge — and that no module under recovery/, evidence/ or providers/claude/ was touched, since those three landed from different tasks whose owners may still be active. Record the runner suite's test count BEFORE and AFTER as explicit numbers; the after count must be greater than or equal to the before count. Then run fresh from the repo root: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck. The daemon typecheck is in the gate deliberately: this surface exists so apps/daemon can compose it into a launcher and restart boundary, and a surface that publishes but does not typecheck from its intended consumer has not done its job. Confirm with wc -l that index.ts and any extracted module are under the 400 hard cap, and record the counts.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Review: is the expected export-name list genuinely hand-written or was it derived from the namespace it checks; does every assertion import the ROOT specifier, with no relative or deep path anywhere in the test; is any test-only module exported; is any name exported twice from two modules; was any module other than index.ts edited; can a consumer actually narrow every published union by its discriminant, proven by calling real functions rather than by constructing literals; did an extracted re-export module get its .js bridge; would the set-equality assertion catch an unreviewed addition as well as a removal. Then stage and commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming only the owned files — never a bare git commit, never git commit -a, never git add -A, and never a directory pathspec under packages/runner/src/, since sibling tasks have uncommitted work throughout this package. Run `git status --porcelain` first and unstage any foreign path with `git restore --staged`. Verify with `git show --stat` that only the owned paths landed. Finally note in the completion evidence that this task publishes the surface only — J3's launcher and restart composition is a separate follow-on and the Foundation canary remains blocked until it lands.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) ONE TASK FOR THREE SUBTREES, despite the 'and' warning: all three land in the SAME two files (index.ts and index-surface.test.ts), share one hand-written export list, and one set-equality assertion. Splitting would mean three tasks editing the same index.ts and the same expected-name list — guaranteed merge conflicts on a shared worktree, for no review benefit.
(2) SIZE IS THE REAL RISK HERE, not correctness. index.ts already carries 126 specifiers; adding three subtrees will very likely push it past the 250-line target. The rail says extract per-area re-export modules rather than letting the entry point sprawl — decide that at step 3 by measuring, not by guessing, and remember an extracted module needs its own .js bridge in the same commit.
(3) CURATED, NOT `export *`. A blanket re-export would publish whatever these modules happen to export next week, which defeats the set-equality assertion that makes the seam a reviewed decision. It would also silently publish test-only helpers.
(4) THE UNION-DISCRIMINABILITY CHECK IS THE ONE NON-MECHANICAL ASSERTION. These subtrees are union-heavy (CrashClassification, OverlapVerdict, ResumeVerdict, DrainAdvance, the evidence result unions), and a consumer that cannot narrow them by discriminant cannot use them at all — the supervisor publish task hit exactly this with LifecycleOutcome, so it is a known failure mode on this seam rather than a hypothetical.

planningNotes.risks:
1. **index.ts will very likely burst the 250-line target.** Measure at step 3 and, if it does, extract per-area re-export modules that index.ts re-exports rather than letting the entry point sprawl toward 400. Any extracted module needs its sibling `.js` bridge in the SAME commit — @moe/runner is bridged and now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate, so an unbridged module fails a gate rather than passing quietly.
2. **Duplicate export names across three subtrees are a compile error.** evidence/ and recovery/ both define failure and layer vocabularies; check for collisions (e.g. a shared `*_LAYERS` or `*Failure` name) before composing, and if two modules genuinely export the same name, that is a finding to report rather than something to paper over with a rename in index.ts.
3. `mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself`: the expected export-name list must be HAND-TRANSCRIBED. If it is generated from Object.keys of the namespace, the test asserts the namespace equals itself and can never fail.
4. **Union discriminability is the known failure mode on this seam.** The supervisor publish task had to prove LifecycleOutcome's three kinds stayed distinguishable through the root. These subtrees are union-heavy; obtain real values by CALLING the exported functions and assert each branch narrows by its discriminant, rather than constructing literals that would typecheck regardless.
5. **Never export a test-only module.** recovery-test-fixtures.ts is the obvious one; check evidence/ and providers/claude/ for others before writing the list.
6. **Do not edit any module other than index.ts.** These three subtrees landed from three different tasks within days; a signature change here would collide with an owner who is still active.
7. The daemon typecheck is in the gate deliberately — this surface exists so apps/daemon can compose it, and a surface that publishes but does not typecheck from its intended consumer has not done its job.
